## The finding `crime_00064` — **Duplicate Component Shape**, medium / confidence 0.70, `duplicate_component_shape.js`, shape hash `e96b55b64336…`, 4 occurrences: | File | Lines | |---|---| | `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` | 142–150 | | `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` | 152–160 | | `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` | 101–109 | | `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` | 112–120 | I read all four sites. The subtree is the **form footer action row** — the last child of `
` in every case: ```tsx
Cancel
``` The four copies are **byte-identical except one string**: the submit label is `Create Invoice` in the create forms and `Edit Invoice` in the edit forms. The cancel href, both class strings, and the ordering are the same everywhere. That's the drift risk: change the cancel button's hover state or the row's gap in one form and the other three silently keep the old look. ## Proposed component `InvoiceFormActions` — a presentational row, no hooks, no handlers, so it works inside either a client or server boundary and needs no `'use client'` of its own. ```tsx // app/ui/invoices/form-actions.tsx import Link from 'next/link'; import { Button } from '@/app/ui/button'; export function InvoiceFormActions({ submitLabel, cancelHref = '/dashboard/invoices', cancelLabel = 'Cancel', children, }: { submitLabel: string; // required — the only real variance today cancelHref?: string; cancelLabel?: string; children?: React.ReactNode; // slot: extra actions, rendered before submit }) { return (
{cancelLabel} {children}
); } ``` **Props:** `submitLabel` (required), `cancelHref`, `cancelLabel`. **Slots:** one — `children`, positioned between cancel and submit, for the destructive/secondary action a future form will want (e.g. a Delete button on the edit form). Deliberately no `className` passthrough: the wrapper's layout classes are the thing being consolidated, so letting call sites override them reopens the drift. Only `submitLabel` is required because it's the only thing that actually differs today. `cancelHref`/`cancelLabel` are defaulted rather than required so the four existing call sites collapse to one line each. Call sites become: ```tsx // create // edit ``` ## Files that would change **New (2)** — `final-example` and `starter-example` are two independent Next.js apps with their own `@/app/*` alias and their own `app/ui/button.tsx`; there's no shared package to hold one copy, so each app gets its own: - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/form-actions.tsx` - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/form-actions.tsx` **Edited (4)** — replace the 9-line block with the one-line call, and drop the now-unused `Link` import where nothing else in the file uses it (worth checking per file; `Button` becomes unused in all four): - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` Six files total. All four edits are at the tail of the file, so no line numbers shift under each other. ## What I left out, and why Directly above each footer sits a second, larger repeated subtree — the status `
` with the pending/paid radios (final `create-form.tsx:88–134`, `edit-form.tsx:96–144`, and the starter equivalents). The detector did **not** flag it, correctly: the edit forms carry `defaultChecked={invoice.status === 'pending'}` and the final create form uses a different input class (`text-white-600 h-4 w-4 …` vs `h-4 w-4 … text-gray-600`), so the shapes genuinely diverge — and that divergence is itself evidence the copies have already drifted. That's a real second extraction (`InvoiceStatusRadios`, props `defaultStatus?: 'pending' | 'paid'` plus the error slot), and it's the one that would also retire `crime_00065`/`crime_00066` — the `"pending"`/`"paid"` literals compared across 4 files in 2 different expression shapes. But it's a larger, behaviour-carrying change with a `state.errors.status` block that differs between the final and starter apps, so I'd land it as a separate commit after the footer extraction rather than bundle the two.
